data.title: bn-3plk: Qualify credential-free native Codex worker boundary

data.body: [HIGH][CWE-770] Rejected-request retention bypasses every global request/byte ceiling. handle() increments and persists each within-per-request body at lines 641-650 and appends a record at line 677 before checking max_requests at lines 690-691; the total-byte check at lines 706-711 charges only an accepted candidate, and snapshot accounting at lines 1009-1018 omits rejected bytes. Focused offline reproduction with max_requests=1 and max_total_bytes=4096 sent twenty GET bodies of 3000 bytes: all returned 405, yet inbound_requests=20, budgeted_request_bytes=0, request_artifacts=20, request_records=20, and evidence grew to 73105 bytes with zero upstream calls. An untrusted worker can grow host evidence and relay memory without bound. Required fix: enforce inbound count and cumulative parsed-byte caps before persistence or record append; include rejected transport/body bytes; bound refusal records/artifacts; close or poison the listener after terminal/budget refusal; add a flood regression asserting bounded file count, bytes, memory, and no upstream call. Failure modes: host disk/RAM exhaustion and incomplete settlement. Edge cases: invalid method/route/model/JSON, duplicate or post-finalized requests, framing errors, a valid request followed by floods, and serial/concurrent connections. Rollback: disable or revert this lane, terminate worker and relay, quarantine partial private evidence, and reject partial receipts. Monitoring: alert on inbound/rejected bytes, record count, evidence growth, or any post-terminal input. Input validation: hard-cap all inbound bytes and records before retention and fail closed.

[MEDIUM][CWE-693] The qualified worker environment is not the claimed complete allowlist. The builder validates only the caller-supplied map at lines 405-411, then emits explicit --env entries without --unsetenv-all at lines 413-440. podman_manifest and settlement re-attest only those argv entries at lines 444-463 and 923-932, not the actual process environment. Fresh offline inspection of the exact cached image ID 28eb0cb65acb65b970e85c0dc57d10067868fae8dd00d072413df273132123ac shows inherited GPG_KEY, PYTHON_VERSION, and PYTHON_SHA256; an ephemeral run with the exact network-none controls also adds HOSTNAME and container. The fresh receipt still reports only the explicit allowlist and valid=true. No provider credential leak was reproduced and the current inherited values are benign build/runtime metadata, but the qualification is false-positive evidence and future image-default proxy, certificate, Python-path, or auth-adjacent variables could affect the worker undetected. Required fix: use --unsetenv-all, explicitly define any unavoidable runtime names, attest /proc/self/environ from the actual worker, reject unexpected or credential-like actual names, and add an image-default canary regression bound to the inspected image/container.

data.body: [LOW][CWE-223] SIGKILL performed while waiting for the direct Codex child is omitted from the teardown receipt. wait_child sends TERM and, after the five-second grace, KILL to the process group, but returns only (status, timed_out). When that KILL removes the direct child and its group, the later quiesce_group call returns (true, false), and line 614 records only that false escalation bit. I reproduced this against the exact pinned supervisor binary 9dfa1e6b263754a379f98dcba970f72a77cd0ca2d34c3ee05dca4d07cb3868e4: a direct fake Codex that ignored TERM produced codex.signal=9 and interrupted_by_signal=15, yet teardown.sigkill_escalated=false and teardown.complete=true; the container was removed and no containers remain. The same omission applies to a TERM-ignoring child at the 900-second timeout. The existing stubborn_group probe misses this path because its direct child exits normally and leaves escalation to quiesce_group. This does not make the failed run successful, hence LOW, but it falsifies retained security evidence and contradicts the documented promise to record escalation. Return an escalation bit from wait_child and OR it with the quiesce_group bit; add direct-child external-TERM and bounded-timeout probes asserting signal 9, sigkill_escalated=true, group quiescence, and container removal.

data.reason: LOW CWE-223: the pinned supervisor can issue SIGKILL to a TERM-ignoring direct Codex child but retain sigkill_escalated=false; dynamic pinned-binary reproduction is in th-2y058j. Preserve the actual escalation bit across wait_child and cover direct-child TERM and timeout paths.
